Script.name: snd
Script.script:
--[[ Search & Destroy — mob/area data layer Sean Stoves, 2026-07-31
The MUSHclient Search_and_Destroy.xml is a 360KB plugin: quest/campaign/gquest target tracking, its own runto, a target miniwindow and a self-updater. Most of the movement half of that is Mudlet's speedwalker's job, so what's ported here is the part nothing else replaces — the mob/area database and the lookups over it.
That database is also what SolaoBot's 'solbot mob <kw>' reads, which is why it lands before the rest of S&D.
Not ported (deliberately): the runto/target automation and the plugin self-updater. See PORTING.md. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.snd = aardkit.snd or {}
local SD = aardkit.snd local U = aardkit.util
local ok, handle = pcall(db.create, db, "aardkitsnd", { mobs = { mob = "", room = "", roomid = 0, zone = "", seen_count = 0, kill_count = 0, _index = { "mob", "zone" }, _unique = { { "mob", "roomid" } }, }, area = { name = "", key = "", minlvl = 0, maxlvl = 0, lock = 0, startRoom = 0, noquest = "", vidblain = "", userKey = "", _index = { "key" }, _unique = { { "key" } }, }, keywords = { area_name = "", mob_name = "", keyword = "", _index = { "mob_name" }, _unique = { { "area_name", "mob_name" } }, }, })
SD.dbh = ok and handle or nil SD.dberr = (not ok) and tostring(handle) or nil
-- lazily resolved, same reason as Loot Tracker's: a nil here reads to every -- consumer as "S&D isn't loaded" and never recovers SD.t = setmetatable({}, { __index = function(_, k) local d = SD.dbh or (db and db.aardkitsnd) return d and d[k] or nil end, })
local T = SD.t
--- -- capture (off by default; the trigger is disabled until 'snd scan on') ---
function SD.on_scan(mob) mob = U.strip_flags(mob) if mob == "" then return end local roomid, room, zone = U.room() if not roomid then return end local where = db:AND(db:eq(T.mobs.mob, mob), db:eq(T.mobs.roomid, roomid)) local found = db:fetch(T.mobs, where) if found and found[1] then U.dbupdate(T.mobs, found[1], { seen_count = (found[1].seen_count or 0) + 1, room = room or "", zone = zone or "" }) else db:add(T.mobs, { mob = mob, room = room or "", roomid = roomid, zone = zone or "", seen_count = 1, kill_count = 0 }) end end
--- -- lookups ---
local function keyword_for(mob) local r = db:fetch(T.keywords, db:eq(T.keywords.mob_name, mob)) return r and r[1] and r[1].keyword or nil end
-- The MUD's own 'where' only sees the area you're standing in, so a miss tells -- you nothing about where the thing actually lives. We have 1795 mobs on record -- with the rooms they were seen in, so answer the question it couldn't. function SD.on_nowhere(term) term = U.trim(term or "") if term == "" then return end local rows = SD.where(term, true) if not rows then U.note("...and nothing matching '" .. term .. "' on record either. 'snd scan on' learns them as you go.") end end
-- quiet = don't complain when there's no match; the caller says something better function SD.where(term, quiet) term = U.trim(term) if term == "" then U.warn("Usage: mobwhere <keyword>"); return end
local rows = db:fetch(T.mobs, db:like(T.mobs.mob, "%" .. term .. "%")) if not rows or #rows == 0 then if not quiet then U.note("Nothing matching '" .. term .. "' on record. The database only knows mobs" .. " it has been shown - 'snd scan on' records them as you walk.") end return nil end
-- merge per mob name so one line covers every room it's been seen in local agg, order = {}, {} for _, r in ipairs(rows) do local nm = U.strip_flags(r.mob) local a = agg[nm] if not a then a = { name = nm, zone = r.zone or "", room = r.room or "", ids = {}, seen = {}, cnt = 0 } agg[nm] = a order[#order + 1] = nm end if r.roomid and r.roomid ~= 0 and not a.seen[r.roomid] then a.seen[r.roomid] = true a.ids[#a.ids + 1] = r.roomid end a.cnt = a.cnt + (r.seen_count or 0) end table.sort(order, function(x, y) return agg[x].cnt > agg[y].cnt end)
U.note(#order .. " mob(s) matching '" .. term .. "' on record:") for i, nm in ipairs(order) do if i > 20 then U.out("\n <#8a93a8>... " .. (#order - 20) .. " more<r>") break end local a = agg[nm] local kw = keyword_for(nm) U.out("\n <#7aa2f7>" .. a.name .. "<r>" .. (kw and (" <#8a93a8>[" .. kw .. "]<r>") or "")) U.out("\n <#c8d0dc>" .. (a.zone ~= "" and a.zone or "?") .. " - " .. (a.room ~= "" and a.room or "?") .. "<r>") local ids = {} for j, id in ipairs(a.ids) do if j > 8 then ids[#ids + 1] = "..."; break end ids[#ids + 1] = U.rid(id) end if #ids > 0 then U.out(" <#8a93a8>rooms: " .. table.concat(ids, ",") .. "<r>") -- clickable: hand the first room to the Mudlet speedwalker U.outLink(" <#3ad07a>[go]<r>", "aardkit.snd.walkto(" .. U.rid(a.ids[1]) .. ")", "Speedwalk to room " .. U.rid(a.ids[1]), true) end end echo("\n") return order end
function SD.walkto(roomid) if not roomExists(roomid) then U.warn("Room " .. U.rid(roomid) .. " isn't in the Mudlet map. Run 'aardmap import yes' first.") return end local here = getPlayerRoom() if not here then U.warn("Mudlet doesn't know where you are yet - move a room and try again.") return end if getPath(here, roomid) then -- SD.walk sends the directions itself; doSpeedWalk() is the stock -- module's override and it mangles this map into bare numbers SD.walk(roomid, nil, U.rid(roomid)) else U.warn("No path from " .. U.rid(here) .. " to " .. U.rid(roomid) .. ".") end end
local function show_area(term) term = U.trim(term):lower() local rows = db:fetch(T.area) if not rows or #rows == 0 then U.note("No area data. Run 'aardkit migrate' to bring it over from MUSHclient.") return end local hits = {} for _, r in ipairs(rows) do if term == "" or (r.name .. " " .. r.key):lower():find(term, 1, true) then hits[#hits + 1] = r end end table.sort(hits, function(a, b) return (a.minlvl or 0) < (b.minlvl or 0) end) U.note(#hits .. " area(s):") for i, r in ipairs(hits) do if i > 40 then U.out("\n <#8a93a8>... " .. (#hits - 40) .. " more<r>") break end U.out(string.format("\n <#7aa2f7>%-32s<r> <#8a93a8>%-14s L%d-%d%s<r>", r.name, r.key, r.minlvl or 0, r.maxlvl or 0, (r.startRoom or 0) > 0 and (" start " .. U.rid(r.startRoom)) or "")) end echo("\n") end
--- -- commands ---
-- Persisted. It was a bare local, so 'snd scan on' lasted until the next -- reload and then quietly went back off - a good part of why the mob table has -- only ever held what the migration put in it. local SCFG = U.load("sndscan", { on = false }) local scan_on = SCFG.on
function SD.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg)
if verb == "" then -- toggle first: SD.paint() now skips the work while the panel's -- hidden, so painting before show() left stale content on screen SD.panel:toggle() SD.paint()
elseif verb == "status" then local m = db:fetch(T.mobs) or {} local a = db:fetch(T.area) or {} local k = db:fetch(T.keywords) or {} U.help("Search & Destroy data", { { "mobs", tostring(#m) }, { "areas", tostring(#a) }, { "keywords", tostring(#k) }, { "scanning", scan_on and "on" or "off" }, })
elseif verb == "cp" or verb == "campaign" then SD.kind = "campaign"; SD.refresh("campaign"); SD.panel:show()
elseif verb == "quest" or verb == "q" then SD.kind = "quest"; SD.refresh("quest"); SD.panel:show()
elseif verb == "gq" or verb == "gquest" then SD.kind = "gquest"; SD.refresh("gquest"); SD.panel:show()
elseif verb == "keywords" or verb == "keys" then SD.keywords()
elseif verb == "hunt" then SD.hunt(rest)
elseif verb == "go" then local n = tonumber(U.trim(rest)) if not n then U.warn("Usage: snd go <number>") else SD.goto_target(SD.kind, n) end
elseif verb == "next" then local i = SD.next_target(SD.kind) if not i then U.note("Nothing left in " .. SD.kind .. ".") else SD.goto_target(SD.kind, i) end
elseif verb == "dock" or verb == "embed" or verb == "hide" or verb == "show" then aardkit.panel.cmd("snd " .. verb)
elseif verb == "mob" or verb == "where" then SD.where(rest)
elseif verb == "area" or verb == "areas" then show_area(rest)
elseif verb == "rewrite" then local v = U.trim(rest):lower() if v == "on" or v == "off" then SD.rewriting(v == "on") U.ok("S&D: campaign list rewritten " .. (v == "on" and "into a clickable block." or "no more - the MUD's own lines stand.")) else U.warn("Usage: snd rewrite on|off (currently " .. (SD.rewriting() and "on" or "off") .. ")") end
elseif verb == "scan" then local v = U.trim(rest):lower() if v == "on" or v == "off" then scan_on = (v == "on") SCFG.on = scan_on U.save("sndscan", SCFG) enableTrigger("scan mob line") if not scan_on then disableTrigger("scan mob line") end U.ok("S&D: room scanning " .. v .. " (and it stays that way).") else U.warn("Usage: snd scan on|off") end
else U.help("Search & Destroy data", { { "snd", "show/hide the target panel" }, { "snd cp | quest | gq", "read your targets and show them" }, { "snd go <n>", "walk to target n" }, { "snd next", "walk to the first one still owed" }, { "ah <mob>", "auto-hunt: follow the MUD's hunt skill to it" }, { "aha", "cancel the hunt" }, { "snd status", "row counts" }, { "snd mob <keyword>", "where a mob has been seen (clickable [go])" }, { "mobwhere <kw>", "same thing, shorter" }, { "snd area [text]", "area list with level ranges and start rooms" }, { "snd keywords", "read 'area keyword' so runto works for unmapped areas" }, { "snd scan on|off", "record mobs from room descriptions as you go" }, { "snd rewrite on|off", "tidy 'cp check' into a clickable list" }, { "" }, { "Click a target in the panel to walk there. The commands are" }, { "here for muscle memory; nobody has to learn them." }, }) end end
-- the trigger ships disabled, so a saved 'on' has to switch it back on if scan_on then tempTimer(1, function() pcall(enableTrigger, "scan mob line") end) end
aardkit.register("snd", "mob/area database from Search & Destroy", SD.cmd)

Script.name: snd/targets
Script.script:
--[[ Search & Destroy — quest / campaign / gquest targets Sean Stoves, 2026-08-01
The MUD tells you what to kill; this remembers it and looks up where it lives in the mob table the data layer already holds. That's the whole job.
Output formats below are the MUD's own, checked against 45 sessions of logs. Earlier versions of this file took them from another plugin's triggers and got them wrong twice over, which is why nothing ever parsed:
You still have to kill * a bartering customer (Fellchantry) <- cp check Find and kill 1 * Islien (Unearthly Bonds) <- cp info You have 6 days, 23 hours and 59 minutes left to finish this campaign.
The bare "* name (area)" an earlier version expected was the MUSHclient S&D plugin's rewrite of the first line, not anything the MUD ever sends.
You are on a quest to slay Eldred the Wise! Eldred the Wise can be found in the vicinity of Training Room which is in the general area of The Witches of Omen Tor. QUEST: You have almost completed your QUEST! <- target is down You inform Alex, the Taskmaster that you have completed your quest.
-----------------------------[ Quest Targets ]--------------------- Kill at least 1 * a bored visitor (The Reception Area). Kill at least 2 * a marsh vole (An odd village among the trees).
Congratulations, that was one of your CAMPAIGN mobs! Congratulations, that was one of the GLOBAL QUEST mobs!
The campaign rows carry their own prefix, so a permanent trigger is safe. The first one opens the capture and the time-remaining line closes it, with a timer behind that in case the block ever ends some way we haven't seen. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.snd = aardkit.snd or {}
local SD = aardkit.snd local U = aardkit.util
-- kind -> ordered list of { name, area, qty, killed } SD.targets = SD.targets or { quest = {}, campaign = {}, gquest = {} } SD.kind = SD.kind or "campaign"
local function list(kind) return SD.targets[kind] or {} end
-- second return says whether this was a new entry; 'cp check' prints one line -- per kill still owed, so the caller needs to tell a repeat from a first sight. local function add(kind, name, area, qty) name = U.trim(name or "") if name == "" then return end local t = list(kind) for _, e in ipairs(t) do if e.name:lower() == name:lower() then return e, false end end t[#t + 1] = { name = name, area = U.trim(area or ""), qty = tonumber(qty) or 1, killed = false } return t[#t], true end
function SD.clear(kind) SD.targets[kind] = {} if SD.paint then SD.paint() end end
--- -- where does it live -- -- The mob table is keyed on the name the MUD prints, but quest text and room -- text don't always agree on articles, so fall back to a keyword match before -- giving up. ---
function SD.locate(name) local T = SD.t if not (T and T.mobs) then return nil end local n = U.trim(name or ""):lower() if n == "" then return nil end
-- db:like reads field.name off the column object. A bare string has no -- .name, so this errored on every call and mob lookup never worked at all. local rows = T.mobs and db:fetch(T.mobs, db:like(T.mobs.mob, n)) or {} if #rows == 0 then local bare = n:gsub("^an? ", ""):gsub("^the ", "") rows = db:fetch(T.mobs, db:like(T.mobs.mob, "%" .. bare .. "%")) end if #rows == 0 then return nil end
table.sort(rows, function(a, b) return (a.seen_count or 0) > (b.seen_count or 0) end) return rows[1] end
-- first one still owed function SD.next_target(kind) for i, e in ipairs(list(kind)) do if not e.killed then return i end end end
--- -- parsing ---
-- What the MUD actually prints, checked against 920 'cp check' blocks in the -- MUSHclient logs: -- -- cp check You still have to kill * a baku (Aardwolf Zoological Park) -- cp info Find and kill 1 * Islien (Unearthly Bonds) -- -- The bare '* name (area)' this used to expect is the MUSHclient S&D plugin's -- own rewrite of the first one, not the MUD - it gagged the line and reprinted -- it. Matching that meant campaign never captured a single target: 6206 of the -- real lines carry the prefix and none carry the bare form. -- -- 'cp check' lists one line per kill still owed, so the same mob twice means a -- 2-kill target rather than a duplicate. -- -- Neither shape carries a header, so the first target line opens the capture -- rather than us arming on a banner or on having sent the command. That way a -- 'cp check' you type yourself lands in the panel exactly like the button's. -- Closed by the time-remaining line, with a timer behind it in case the block -- ends some way we haven't seen.
local cp_timer local capturing = false local gagged = false local print_block
local TCFG = U.load("sndtargets", { rewrite = true })
local function cp_stop() local was = capturing capturing = false if cp_timer then killTimer(cp_timer); cp_timer = nil end -- Only if we actually swallowed the lines, or a bare cp_stop would reprint -- the last campaign out of nowhere. if was and gagged and print_block then print_block() end gagged = false if SD.paint then SD.paint() end end
SD.cp_stop = cp_stop
local function cp_start() SD.kind = "campaign" -- if a block is already mid-flight (some lines gagged/deleted already, -- closing 'time remaining' line not in yet) a re-check hitting this again -- - the panel's button, or 'cp info' banner firing while 'cp check' output -- is still streaming - used to wipe the array out from under the capture -- in progress and lose what it already swallowed. Just buy it more time -- instead of clearing what's there. if capturing then if cp_timer then killTimer(cp_timer) end cp_timer = tempTimer(12, cp_stop) return end SD.targets.campaign = {} capturing = true gagged = false cp_timer = tempTimer(12, cp_stop) end
SD.arm_campaign = cp_start
--- -- rewriting the list -- -- 'cp check' is fifteen lines of prose with the two things you actually want - -- which mob, and where it lives - buried in the middle of a sentence: -- -- You still have to kill * a bartering customer (Fellchantry) -- -- so the lines get swallowed and reprinted as a block you can act on: -- -- 1 a bartering customer Fellchantry [go] [hunt] -- -- As a block and not line by line, because the count only becomes knowable at -- the end: the MUD prints the same mob twice when it still owes two, and there -- is no way to go back and amend a line already on screen. -- -- [go] is the same walk chain the panel's rows use. [hunt] sends the MUD's own -- hunt skill. Neither chains into a kill - see the note on 'help policies7' in -- walk.lua. ---
-- 'hunt' wants one keyword, not a sentence. Drop a leading article, drop any -- trailing prepositional phrase, and take the last word - that lands on the -- noun most of the time, and without the phrase strip "a screaming ghost bent -- on vengeance" would go hunting for 'vengeance' instead of 'ghost'. -- -- Still a guess. The tooltip shows exactly what will be sent, and if it's wrong -- you type 'ah <keyword>' yourself. local TAIL = { " bent on ", " of ", " in ", " from ", " with ", " on " }
local function huntkey(name) local s = tostring(name or ""):gsub("^[Tt]he%s+", ""):gsub("^[Aa]n?%s+", "") for _, sep in ipairs(TAIL) do local cut = s:lower():find(sep, 1, true) if cut then s = s:sub(1, cut - 1); break end end return (s:match("([%w'-]+)%s*$") or s):lower() end
-- ui.lua needs the same answer for its buttons. It used to keep a second copy -- and the copy had %%s where it wanted %s, so it silently returned the whole -- name. One definition, no drift. SD.huntkey = huntkey
function print_block() local t = list("campaign") if #t == 0 then return end
U.out(string.format("\n<#e0af68>Campaign<r> <#8a93a8>%d still to kill<r>", #t)) for i, e in ipairs(t) do local key = huntkey(e.name) U.out(string.format("\n<#8a93a8>%3d<r> <#c8d0dc>%-36s<r> <#7aa2f7>%-30s<r>", i, e.name .. ((e.qty or 1) > 1 and (" x" .. e.qty) or ""), e.area)) U.outLink(" <#3ad07a>[go]<r>", string.format("aardkit.snd.goto_target(%q, %d)", "campaign", i), "Walk to " .. e.name) U.outLink(" <#e0af68>[hunt]<r>", string.format("aardkit.snd.hunt(%q)", key), "hunt " .. key) end echo("\n") end
function SD.on_cp_target(name, area) if not capturing then cp_start() end if TCFG.rewrite then U.gag(); gagged = true end local e, isnew = add("campaign", name, area, 1) if e and not isnew then e.qty = (e.qty or 1) + 1 end -- cp_stop() repaints once the block closes - a 'cp check' streams 10-15 -- lines, and painting on every single one is a full redraw of all 3 tabs -- and every visible row for something the user can't even see mid-stream end
function SD.rewriting(v) if v ~= nil then TCFG.rewrite = v and true or false; U.save("sndtargets", TCFG) end return TCFG.rewrite end
-- 'cp info' banner. Only useful as an early reset - the target lines that -- follow would have opened the capture on their own anyway. function SD.on_cp_header() cp_start() end
-- 'cp check' with nothing running answers "You are not currently on a -- campaign." and no target lines, which used to leave the capture armed for its -- full 12 seconds and the panel showing "nothing tracked" with no idea whether -- it had failed or you simply had no campaign. Say which. function SD.on_cp_none() SD.targets.campaign = {} SD.kind = "campaign" cp_stop() U.note("No campaign running. 'campaign request' at a questor starts one.") end
-- 'quest request' answers in the questmaster's own voice, wrapped in tells and -- word-wrapped wherever your screen happens to break: -- -- Alex, the Taskmaster tells you 'Seek a flock of copper birds out somewhere in the vicinity' -- Alex, the Taskmaster tells you 'of Dark Pwyll which is in the general area' -- Alex, the Taskmaster tells you 'of Annwn.' -- -- The mob, the room and the area are all in there, split across lines at points -- that move with your wrap setting. Matching that is a losing game. 'quest info' -- says the same thing in three fixed lines we already parse, so the grant just -- asks for it - and since the panel is about to show it, the answer is gagged. -- -- Three questmasters appear in the logs (Alex the Taskmaster, Questor, Wolfie), -- so the trigger can't name one. The time-remaining line is the last thing every -- grant prints and it says the same words regardless of who said it. local autoq = false local autoq_t
local function autoq_off() autoq = false if autoq_t then killTimer(autoq_t); autoq_t = nil end end
function SD.on_quest_granted() autoq_off() autoq = true -- if the reply never lands, stop gagging rather than eating quest lines -- you typed for yourself later autoq_t = tempTimer(6, autoq_off) send("quest info", false) end
function SD.on_quest_target(name) if autoq then U.gag() end SD.targets.quest = {} add("quest", name, "", 1) SD.kind = "quest" if SD.paint then SD.paint() end end
-- "<mob> can be found in the vicinity of <room> which" function SD.on_quest_room(room) if autoq then U.gag() end local e = list("quest")[1] if e then e.room = U.trim(room or "") end if SD.paint then SD.paint() end end
-- "is in the general area of <area>." function SD.on_quest_area(area) if autoq then U.gag() end autoq_off() -- last line of the reply local e = list("quest")[1] if e then e.area = U.trim(area or "") end if SD.paint then SD.paint() end if SD.panel then SD.panel:show() end end
function SD.on_gq_target(qty, name, room) local e = add("gquest", name, "", qty) if e then e.room = U.trim(room or "") end SD.kind = "gquest" if SD.paint then SD.paint() end end
function SD.on_gq_header() SD.targets.gquest = {} SD.kind = "gquest" end
function SD.on_cp_done() SD.targets.campaign = {} U.ok("Campaign complete.") if SD.paint then SD.paint() end end
-- "QUEST: You have almost completed your QUEST!" is the MUD saying the target is -- down and the questmaster is owed a visit - it is the closest thing a plain -- quest has to the campaign kill line, so use it as one. function SD.on_quest_killed() for _, e in ipairs(list("quest")) do e.killed = true end if SD.paint then SD.paint() end end
function SD.on_quest_done() SD.targets.quest = {} if SD.paint then SD.paint() end end
-- The congratulations line doesn't name what you killed, so read back up the -- buffer for the death line that came with it. Cheaper and more honest than -- re-sending 'campaign check' after every kill. -- -- Aardwolf has dozens of finishing-move flavor lines - "collapses as the life -- is hammered out of him", "the acidic venom flays X's skin from his bones", -- "the final deadly circle turns X into food for the worms" - and chasing all -- of them with regexes is a losing game. What we actually need is simpler: -- does one of the lines we just saw report a death AND name a mob we're still -- owed? That also dodges the level-up/skillgain spam XP dumps between the -- death line and the congratulations line - checked against the play logs -- that gap runs past 10 lines (level-up + 2 skill gains), so this looks back -- 30 instead of the 6 that missed it. local DEATH_MARK = { "is dead", "is slain by" }
function SD.on_camp_kill(kind) local n = getLineNumber and getLineNumber() if not n then return end local lines = getLines(math.max(0, n - 30), n) or {} for i = #lines, 1, -1 do local low = lines[i]:lower() local isdeath = false for _, m in ipairs(DEATH_MARK) do if low:find(m, 1, true) then isdeath = true; break end end if isdeath then for _, e in ipairs(list(kind)) do if not e.killed and low:find(e.name:lower(), 1, true) then SD.on_kill(e.name, kind) return end end end end end
-- Ticks a target off by name. Called from the campaign/gquest kill lines above. function SD.on_kill(name, kind) name = U.trim(name or ""):lower() if name == "" then return end local hit = false for k, t in pairs(SD.targets) do if not kind or k == kind then for _, e in ipairs(t) do if not e.killed and (e.name:lower() == name or e.name:lower():find(name, 1, true) or name:find(e.name:lower(), 1, true)) then e.killed = true hit = true end end end end if hit and SD.paint then SD.paint() end end
--- -- counts, for the tab labels ---
function SD.counts(kind) local t, done = list(kind), 0 for _, e in ipairs(t) do if e.killed then done = done + 1 end end return done, #t end

Script.name: snd/hunt
Script.script:
--[[ Search & Destroy — auto-hunt Sean Stoves, 2026-08-01
'ah <mob>' follows the MUD's own hunt skill to a target, one room at a time. The loop is: hunt, read the direction, move, hunt again, until the mob is in the room with you.
This is the piece 'snd go' can't do. That walks the Mudlet mapper, so it needs the room already in your map; hunt works in areas you've never seen.
The message formats are the MUD's. Two are worth knowing about:
You are confident that a sea snake passed through here, heading north. You are almost certain that a sea snake is north from here.
and the three low-skill variants ("the trail is confusing", "there are traces of", "you have no idea what you're doing") deliberately ABORT rather than being followed. Under 85% hunt skill the direction is a guess, and following a guess walks you somewhere random.
Safety, because this moves you around the world on its own: - never runs while you're flagged AFK, same gate as everything else here - a hard step cap, so a hunt that loops can't walk forever - stops dead on anything it doesn't recognise rather than pressing on ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.snd = aardkit.snd or {}
local SD = aardkit.snd local U = aardkit.util
local CFG = U.load("sndhunt", { gap = 0.4, maxsteps = 120 })
local trigs, mob, steps, lastdir = {}, nil, 0, nil local opening = false -- mid door-open, so a stray 'You open' can't move us local rehunt_t -- pending 0.4s re-hunt timer from step(), see SD.hunt_stop()
local function untrig() for _, id in ipairs(trigs) do pcall(killTrigger, id) end trigs = {} end
local function arm(pat, fn) trigs[#trigs + 1] = tempRegexTrigger(pat, fn) end
function SD.hunting() return mob ~= nil end
function SD.hunt_stop(why, good) if not mob then return end local m = mob untrig() -- SD.hunt() reassigns mob to the NEW target right after this returns, and -- the guard in step()'s timer only checks "if mob" - a stale timer from -- the OLD hunt would still be armed and would fire "hunt <new mob>" early if rehunt_t then killTimer(rehunt_t); rehunt_t = nil end mob, steps, lastdir, opening = nil, 0, nil, false if good then U.ok("Auto-hunt: found " .. m .. ".") elseif why then U.warn("Auto-hunt: stopped - " .. why .. ".") end end
local function step(dir) if not mob then return end steps = steps + 1 if steps > CFG.maxsteps then SD.hunt_stop("gave up after " .. CFG.maxsteps .. " rooms") return end if aardkit.whopoll and aardkit.whopoll.afk then SD.hunt_stop("you're flagged AFK") return end lastdir = dir send(dir, false) if rehunt_t then killTimer(rehunt_t) end rehunt_t = tempTimer(CFG.gap, function() rehunt_t = nil if mob then send("hunt " .. mob, false) end end) end
function SD.hunt(name) name = U.trim(name or "") if name == "" then U.warn("Usage: ah <mob> ('aha' or 'ah stop' to cancel)") return end local low = name:lower() if low == "stop" or low == "abort" or low == "cancel" or low == "0" then SD.hunt_stop("cancelled") return end if aardkit.whopoll and aardkit.whopoll.afk then U.warn("Auto-hunt: not while you're flagged AFK.") return end
SD.hunt_stop() mob, steps, lastdir, opening = name, 0, nil, false U.note("Auto-hunt: after " .. name .. "...")
-- the two readings that mean the trail is solid arm([[^You are confident that .+ passed through here, heading (north|south|east|west|up|down)\.$]], function() step(matches[2]) end) arm([[^You are (?:almost )?certain that .+ is (north|south|east|west|up|down) from here\.$]], function() step(matches[2]) end)
-- arrived - anchored to the mob actually being hunted. The MUD prints an -- "X is here!" line for every mob in the room, not just the one hunted - -- grep the play logs and "A bandit is here!" turns up as an ordinary room -- bystander with no hunt anywhere nearby - so this used to stop the hunt -- on whatever mob happened to be co-located. Building a regex out of a -- MUD-typed keyword risks apostrophes/parens in the name breaking the -- pattern, so match the line generically and check the name ourselves. arm([[^.+ is here!$]], function() if matches[1] and matches[1]:lower():find(low, 1, true) then SD.hunt_stop(nil, true) end end)
-- Under 85% hunt skill the MUD hedges, and the direction it gives is a -- guess. Following a guess is how you end up three areas away. arm([[^(?:The trail of .+ is confusing|There are traces of .+ having been here|You have no idea what you're doing)]], function() SD.hunt_stop("hunt skill too low to trust the trail") end)
-- portals need a command we can't infer; hand it back rather than guess arm([[^You are (?:almost )?certain that .+ is through .+\.$]], function() SD.hunt_stop("the trail goes through a portal - take it yourself") end) arm([[^You are confident that .+ passed through here, heading through .+\.$]], function() SD.hunt_stop("the trail goes through a portal - take it yourself") end)
-- A shut door is worth one 'open' in the direction we were already headed. -- Going back through step() rather than sending the move directly keeps the -- step cap and the AFK gate on the door path too - it's the same move. arm([[^The .+ is closed\.$]], function() if lastdir then opening = true send("open " .. lastdir, false) end end) arm([[^You open .+\.$]], function() if mob and opening and lastdir then opening = false step(lastdir) end end)
arm([[^You do not have a key for .+\.$]], function() SD.hunt_stop("locked door and no key") end) arm([[^Magical wards around .+ bounce you back\.$]], function() SD.hunt_stop("warded room") end)
arm([[^(?:No one in this area by (?:the name '.+'|that name)\.|You couldn't find a path to .+ from here\.|You seem unable to hunt that target for some reason\.)$]], function() SD.hunt_stop("the MUD can't hunt that here") end) arm([[^(?:Not while you are fighting!|You can't hunt while (?:resting|sitting)\.|You dream about going on a nice hunting trip)]], function() SD.hunt_stop("can't hunt right now") end)
send("hunt " .. mob, false) end
function SD.huntcmd(verb, rest) if verb == "hunt" then SD.hunt(rest) return true end return false end
-- a hunt in progress means nothing once the connection drops U.killhandler(aardkit_snd_hunt_disc) aardkit_snd_hunt_disc = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysDisconnectionEvent", function() SD.hunt_stop() end)

Script.name: snd/walk
Script.script:
--[[ Search & Destroy — walking to a target Sean Stoves, 2026-08-01
Clicking a target should just get you there. What that takes depends on how much we already know, so it's a chain that stops as soon as it can:
1. know the exact room -> walk straight to it 2. know a room NAME -> look it up in the map, prefer the target's area 3. know only the area -> walk to the area's start room, then ask the MUD 'where <mob>', and walk to whatever it names
Step 3 is the one that matters, and it's why S&D kept a start room per area: the mapper can't run you to an area, only to a room, so you need one room in that area to aim at first. Our area table carries those already.
'where' only reports the room the mob is in right now and only works inside the area, which is exactly why it comes after the move rather than before.
where huge cat a huge cat Kittens' playroom There is no viper around here.
Mudlet has no speedwalk-finished event, so arrival is detected off gmcp.room.info with a timeout behind it.
We do NOT call gotoRoom(). The AardwolfMudlet module overrides doSpeedWalk(), and Mudlet's gotoRoom routes through that override - its buildSpeedWalk() merges getRoomExits with getSpecialExitsSwap and then looks the merged keys up in a short-direction table that doesn't have them, so on this map it sent bare numbers ("3") instead of directions.
Instead: getPath() fills speedWalkDir with direction names, and we hand those to the MUD's own 'run' command as 'run 3n2e2s'. Per 'help run' that is better than sending directions one at a time - less spam, the map keeps up, tells are saved for replay, and the MUD aborts by itself after three failed moves.
'run' takes the six basic directions ONLY: no diagonals, no doors, no custom exits. So the path is split into runs of basic directions with anything else sent on its own, in order. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.snd = aardkit.snd or {}
local SD = aardkit.snd local U = aardkit.util
local WCFG = U.load("sndwalk", { arrive = 45, where = 4, gap = 0.25 })
local arrive_h, arrive_t, where_trigs, where_t, step_t
local function drop_arrive() -- registered through core rather than as a raw handler, so it goes through -- the same change-diff as everything else; unwatch is the teardown aardkit.gmcp.unwatch("sndwalk") if arrive_h then U.killhandler(arrive_h); arrive_h = nil end if arrive_t then killTimer(arrive_t); arrive_t = nil end -- the per-step send timers below were never tracked, so switching targets -- (or walk_stop()) mid-walk left the old walk's queued moves live - they'd -- fire later and get sent as if they belonged to whatever walk was current -- at the time, since the guard inside only checked the shared arrive_h for _, id in ipairs(step_t or {}) do pcall(killTimer, id) end step_t = nil end
local function drop_where() for _, id in ipairs(where_trigs or {}) do pcall(killTrigger, id) end where_trigs = nil if where_t then killTimer(where_t); where_t = nil end end
function SD.walk_stop() drop_arrive(); drop_where() end
--- -- walk to a room id and call back on arrival ---
function SD.walk(dest, cb, what) dest = tonumber(dest) if not dest or not roomExists(dest) then U.warn("S&D: room " .. tostring(dest) .. " isn't in the map.") return false end
local here = getPlayerRoom and getPlayerRoom() if here == dest then if cb then cb() end return true end if not here then U.warn("S&D: Mudlet doesn't know which room you're in yet - move once and retry.") return false end -- must actually run: speedWalkDir is whatever the LAST getPath left behind if not getPath(here, dest) then U.warn("S&D: no path from here to " .. (what or U.rid(dest)) .. ".") return false end
-- getPath filled speedWalkDir for us; copy it before anything else can local steps = {} for i, d in ipairs(speedWalkDir or {}) do steps[i] = d end if #steps == 0 then U.warn("S&D: no route to " .. (what or U.rid(dest)) .. ".") return false end local cmds = SD.compress(steps)
drop_arrive() aardkit.snd.on_arrive = function() if (getPlayerRoom and getPlayerRoom()) == dest then drop_arrive() if cb then cb() end end end -- immediate: arriving is what ends the walk, and a second's wait there -- would have the next step sent from the room we just left aardkit.gmcp.watch("sndwalk", "room.info", "aardkit.snd.on_arrive", true) arrive_t = tempTimer(WCFG.arrive, function() drop_arrive() U.warn("S&D: gave up waiting to reach " .. (what or U.rid(dest)) .. ".") end)
U.note("Walking " .. #steps .. " room(s) to " .. (what or U.rid(dest)) .. " (" .. #cmds .. " command" .. (#cmds == 1 and "" or "s") .. ").") step_t = {} for i, c in ipairs(cmds) do step_t[#step_t + 1] = tempTimer(WCFG.gap * (i - 1), function() if arrive_h then send(c, false) end -- stops the moment we arrive end) end return true end
-- 'run' handles the six basic directions and nothing else, so fold consecutive -- basic steps into one 'run 3n2e2s' and leave everything else - diagonals, doors, -- portals, custom exits - as its own command, in order. local BASIC = { north = "n", south = "s", east = "e", west = "w", up = "u", down = "d" }
function SD.compress(steps) local out, buf = {}, {}
local function flush() if #buf == 0 then return end local parts, i = {}, 1 while i <= #buf do local d, n = buf[i], 1 while buf[i + n] == d do n = n + 1 end parts[#parts + 1] = (n > 1 and n or "") .. d i = i + n end -- one hop is just the direction; 'run n' is noise out[#out + 1] = (#buf == 1) and buf[1] or ("run " .. table.concat(parts)) buf = {} end
for _, d in ipairs(steps) do local b = BASIC[d] if b then buf[#buf + 1] = b else flush(); out[#out + 1] = d end end flush() return out end
--- -- resolve a room NAME to an id, preferring the target's own area ---
function SD.find_room(name, areaname) name = U.trim(name or "") if name == "" then return nil end
local ok, hits = pcall(searchRoom, name) if not ok or type(hits) ~= "table" then return nil end
local want if areaname and areaname ~= "" then for an, aid in pairs(getAreaTable and getAreaTable() or {}) do if an:lower() == areaname:lower() or an:lower():find(areaname:lower(), 1, true) then want = aid; break end end end
local first for k, v in pairs(hits) do -- searchRoom's shape moved between Mudlet versions: sometimes -- id -> name, sometimes name -> id. Take whichever side is a room. local id = tonumber(k) or tonumber(v) if id and roomExists(id) then first = first or id if want and getRoomArea(id) == want then return id end end end return first end
-- one room to aim at inside an area: our own start room, else anything in it function SD.area_room(areaname) areaname = U.trim(areaname or "") if areaname == "" then return nil end
local T = SD.t if T and T.area then local rows = db:fetch(T.area, db:like(T.area.name, "%" .. areaname .. "%")) for _, r in ipairs(rows or {}) do local s = tonumber(r.startRoom) if s and s > 0 and roomExists(s) then return s, r.name end end end
for an, aid in pairs(getAreaTable and getAreaTable() or {}) do if an:lower() == areaname:lower() or an:lower():find(areaname:lower(), 1, true) then for _, id in pairs(getAreaRooms(aid) or {}) do return id, an end end end end
--- -- area keywords, straight from 'area keyword' -- -- The mapper walks you to a ROOM. When we have no room in an area - never been -- there, or the import missed it - the MUD's own 'runto <keyword>' still works, -- so keep the keyword list. Captured rather than hardcoded: it's ~280 areas and -- it changes when areas are added. -- -- 150 170 130 chantry Fellchantry ---
local key_trig, key_timer, key_n
function SD.keys_stop() if key_trig then killTrigger(key_trig); key_trig = nil end if key_timer then killTimer(key_timer); key_timer = nil end if key_n then U.ok("S&D: learned " .. key_n .. " area keyword(s).") ; key_n = nil end end
function SD.keywords() local T = SD.t if not (T and T.area) then U.warn("S&D: no database."); return end SD.keys_stop() key_n = 0 U.note("S&D: reading area keywords...") key_trig = tempRegexTrigger([[^\s*(\d+)\s+(\d+)\s+(\d*)\s+(\S+)\s\s+(\S.*?)\s*$]], function() local minl, maxl, lock, k, name = matches[2], matches[3], matches[4], matches[5], matches[6] local rows = db:fetch(T.area, db:eq(T.area.name, name)) if rows and rows[1] then U.dbupdate(T.area, rows[1], { key = k, minlvl = tonumber(minl), maxlvl = tonumber(maxl), lock = tonumber(lock) or 0 }) else db:add(T.area, { name = name, key = k, minlvl = tonumber(minl), maxlvl = tonumber(maxl), lock = tonumber(lock) or 0, startRoom = 0, noquest = "", vidblain = "", userKey = "" }) end key_n = (key_n or 0) + 1 end) key_timer = tempTimer(15, SD.keys_stop) send("area keyword", false) end
-- the keyword for an area name, if we've learned it function SD.area_key(areaname) local T = SD.t if not (T and T.area) or not areaname or areaname == "" then return nil end local rows = db:fetch(T.area, db:like(T.area.name, "%" .. areaname .. "%")) for _, r in ipairs(rows or {}) do if r.key and r.key ~= "" then return r.key, r.name end end end
--- -- ask the MUD where the mob is, right now, in this area -- -- NOT SD.where. That name belongs to the database lookup in init.lua, and this -- file loads after it, so defining both meant this one silently won and every -- caller expecting the database got a command sent to the MUD instead. The -- database lookup for a failed 'where' then answered a failed 'where' by -- sending another one, forever. ---
function SD.ask_where(mob, cb) -- mob is raw text the MUD printed back to us (targets.lua's add() only -- U.trim()s it) and send() honours Mudlet's command separator, not just -- ALIAS matching - a mob name that happened to contain it would smuggle a -- second command in on the tail of 'where'. 'where' takes free text -- ("kul tiras", "dirty old man") so unlike the hunt/kill buttons this -- can't collapse to one keyword; just strip the separator itself. local sep = getCommandSeparator and getCommandSeparator() or ";" if sep ~= "" then mob = (mob or ""):gsub(sep:gsub("(%W)", "%%%1"), " ") end mob = U.trim(mob)
drop_where() where_trigs = {} local done = false
local function finish(room) if done then return end done = true drop_where() cb(room) end
-- "a huge cat Kittens' playroom" where_trigs[#where_trigs + 1] = tempRegexTrigger( [[^(\S.{0,28}?)\s\s+(\S.*?)\s*$]], function() finish(matches[3]) end) where_trigs[#where_trigs + 1] = tempRegexTrigger( [[^There is no .+ around here\.$]], function() finish(nil) end)
where_t = tempTimer(WCFG.where, function() finish(nil) end) send("where " .. mob, false) end
--- -- the click ---
function SD.goto_target(kind, i) local t = SD.targets[kind] or {} local e = t[i] if not e then U.warn("No target " .. tostring(i) .. " in " .. kind .. "."); return end
SD.walk_stop()
-- 1. a room id we already know, from the mob database local row = SD.locate(e.name) if row and tonumber(row.roomid) and tonumber(row.roomid) > 0 and roomExists(tonumber(row.roomid)) then U.ok("-> " .. e.name .. " " .. (row.room or "?") .. " " .. U.rid(row.roomid)) SD.walk(tonumber(row.roomid), nil, e.name) return end
-- 2. a room name, which quests hand us outright if e.room and e.room ~= "" then local id = SD.find_room(e.room, e.area) if id then U.ok("-> " .. e.name .. " " .. e.room .. " " .. U.rid(id)) SD.walk(id, nil, e.name) return end end
-- 3. only an area: get into it, then ask the MUD where the mob is local start, aname = SD.area_room(e.area) if not start then -- Nothing in the map for that area, so fall back on the MUD's own runto. -- It only works from Aylor recall unless you've set a runprefix, and it -- stops there: no hunt, no kill. Chaining those together automatically is -- botting and against the rules - see 'help policies7'. local k, kn = SD.area_key(e.area) if k then U.note("Not in the map - sending 'runto " .. k .. "' (" .. (kn or e.area) .. "). Needs Aylor recall or a runprefix.") U.note("Then 'where " .. e.name .. "' yourself, or click again once you're there.") send("runto " .. k, false) else U.warn("S&D: don't know where '" .. e.name .. "' is" .. (e.area ~= "" and (", and '" .. e.area .. "' isn't in the map") or "") .. ". Try 'snd keywords' to learn the area list.") end return end
U.note("-> " .. (aname or e.area) .. ", then asking where " .. e.name .. " is...") SD.walk(start, function() SD.ask_where(e.name, function(room) if not room then U.warn("S&D: 'where' didn't find " .. e.name .. " in this area.") return end e.room = room local id = SD.find_room(room, e.area) if not id then U.note("S&D: " .. e.name .. " is in '" .. room .. "' - not in the map, walk it yourself.") if SD.paint then SD.paint() end return end U.ok("-> " .. e.name .. " " .. room .. " " .. U.rid(id)) if SD.paint then SD.paint() end SD.walk(id, nil, e.name) end) end, aname or e.area) end
U.killhandler(aardkit_snd_walk_disc) aardkit_snd_walk_disc = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysDisconnectionEvent", function() SD.walk_stop() end)

Script.name: snd/ui
Script.script:
--[[ Search & Destroy — panel Sean Stoves, 2026-08-01 The MUSHclient plugin drives everything through about twenty-five terse aliases: xq, cp ch, gq i, ht, qw, nx, nx-, go 3, xrt, qk, aha, xg ref. They all made sense to whoever wrote them and none of them are guessable. So: three tabs, a scrolling list, and a row of buttons. Clicking a target selects it and does nothing else. What happens next is a button, one press per action - [hunt] asks the MUD which way it is, [attack] swings at it, [go] walks. Nothing chains into anything, which is the line between a client that saves you typing and one that plays for you. ]] aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.snd = aardkit.snd or {} local SD = aardkit.snd local U = aardkit.util local TAB_H, ROW_H, PAD = 24, 22, 4 local BTN_H, SEL_H = 22, 18 local COL = { bg = "#0d1117", tab = "#1b2540", tabon = "#274060", row = "#141b2d", hover = "#274060", text = "#c8d0dc", dim = "#8a93a8", done = "#3ad07a", sel = "#2d3d5c", btn = "#1b2540", accent = "#e94560", border = "#3a4a6b", } local KINDS = { "quest", "campaign", "gquest" } local LABEL = { quest = "Quest", campaign = "Campaign", gquest = "GQuest" } local SHORT = { quest = "Q", campaign = "CP", gquest = "GQ" } -- widget caches, declared ahead of panel.new() below so its onbuild closure -- closes over these locals and not globals of the same name local tabs, rows, foot = {}, {}, nil local seltxt, btns = nil, {} local panel = aardkit.panel.new({ name = "snd", title = "Search & Destroy", x = "10px", y = "560px", width = 380, height = 300, consoleless = true, -- laid out by hand, so it has to be told when the panel changes size onresize = function() if aardkit.snd.paint then aardkit.snd.paint() end end, -- Panel:_build() swaps panel.container for a brand-new Geyser object on -- every dock/embed switch, but tab_label/row_label/button below cache -- their Labels by hand and were never told - a mode switch left them -- pointing at widgets inside the OLD, now-hidden container, and paint()'s -- "if not cached, make one" kept right on reusing the orphaned ones. onbuild = function() tabs, rows, btns, seltxt = {}, {}, {}, nil if aardkit.snd.paint then aardkit.snd.paint() end end, }) SD.panel = panel -- which row the buttons act on. Kept per tab so switching tabs and back doesn't -- lose your place. Keyed on the target's NAME, not its index - cp_start() and -- on_quest_target() wipe and rebuild SD.targets[kind] on every re-check, and -- the MUD doesn't promise the same order back, so an index picked before a -- refresh can point at a different mob after one. A name survives the rebuild. SD.aim = SD.aim or {} -- first visible row per tab; the list is a window onto the targets, not all of them SD.top = SD.top or {} function SD.aimed() local nm = SD.aim[SD.kind] if not nm then return nil end for i, e in ipairs(SD.targets[SD.kind] or {}) do if e.name == nm then return e, i end end -- the mob it pointed at is gone - killed, or fell out on a refresh SD.aim[SD.kind] = nil end local function style(bg, border) return string.format( "background-color: %s; border: 1px solid %s; border-radius: 3px;", bg, border or COL.border) end local function width() local c = panel.container local w = c and U.px(c.get_width and c:get_width() or c.width) or 360 return w < 60 and 360 or w end --- -- clicks --- function SD.on_tab(kind) SD.kind = kind SD.top[kind] = SD.top[kind] or 1 SD.paint() end -- Selecting is all a row click does. It used to walk you there, which meant a -- misclick sent you across the world. -- -- The callback gets a slot, not a target index, because the list scrolls - slot -- 1 is whatever is at the top right now. function SD.on_rowclick(slot) local p = SD.page or { first = 1 } SD.on_row((p.first or 1) + (tonumber(slot) or 1) - 1) end function SD.on_row(i) local e = (SD.targets[SD.kind] or {})[i] if not e then return end SD.aim[SD.kind] = (SD.aim[SD.kind] == e.name) and nil or e.name SD.paint() end local function scrollby(n) local t = SD.targets[SD.kind] or {} local p = SD.page or { fits = 1 } SD.top[SD.kind] = math.min(math.max(1, (SD.top[SD.kind] or 1) + n), math.max(1, #t - (p.fits or 1) + 1)) SD.paint() end function SD.on_up() scrollby(-(SD.page and SD.page.fits or 1)) end function SD.on_down() scrollby(SD.page and SD.page.fits or 1) end function SD.on_refresh() SD.refresh(SD.kind) end --- -- the buttons -- -- One press, one command. 'hunt' asks the MUD which way it is and stops there; -- the room-by-room walker is still 'ah ' typed on purpose. --- -- One definition, shared. targets.lua owns it because that's where the output -- block needs it too; this file had its own copy and the copy was wrong - -- written with %%s and %%w, which in a Lua pattern is a literal percent sign, -- so nothing ever matched and the buttons sent the whole mob name. local keyword = SD.huntkey SD.keyword = keyword local function need_aim() local e, i = SD.aimed() if not e then U.warn("S&D: click a target in the panel first."); return nil end return e, i end function SD.on_hunt() local e = need_aim(); if not e then return end send("hunt " .. keyword(e.name), false) end function SD.on_attack() local e = need_aim(); if not e then return end send("kill " .. keyword(e.name), false) end function SD.on_go() local _, i = need_aim(); if not i then return end SD.goto_target(SD.kind, i) end --- -- paint --- local function tab_label(i, kind) local name = "aardkit_snd_tab" .. i .. "_" .. (panel.gen or 1) if not tabs[i] then tabs[i] = Geyser.Label:new({ name = name, x = 0, y = 0, width = 10, height = TAB_H }, panel.container) tabs[i]:setClickCallback("aardkit.snd.on_tab", kind) end return tabs[i] end -- Geyser.ScrollBox was tried here and is wrong for this: nested inside an -- Adjustable.Container it draws its scrollbar against the main window rather -- than the panel, and the rows and buttons land outside the frame. So the list -- is plain labels with an offset, and the arrows page it. Everything stays a -- child of the container, which is the thing that nests correctly. local function row_label(i) local name = "aardkit_snd_row" .. i .. "_" .. (panel.gen or 1) if not rows[i] then rows[i] = Geyser.Label:new({ name = name, x = 0, y = 0, width = 10, height = ROW_H - 2 }, panel.container) rows[i]:setClickCallback("aardkit.snd.on_rowclick", i) end return rows[i] end local function button(key, label, cb, x, w, y) if not btns[key] then btns[key] = Geyser.Label:new({ name = "aardkit_snd_btn_" .. key .. "_" .. (panel.gen or 1), x = 0, y = 0, width = 10, height = BTN_H - 2, }, panel.container) btns[key]:setClickCallback(cb) end local b = btns[key] b:move(x, y) b:resize(w, BTN_H - 2) return b end function SD.paint() if not panel.container then return end if not panel:visible() then return end -- hidden panel, skip the Geyser work local w = width() local tw = math.floor((w - PAD * 4) / #KINDS) for i, kind in ipairs(KINDS) do local l = tab_label(i, kind) local done, total = SD.counts(kind) local on = (SD.kind == kind) l:move(PAD + (i - 1) * (tw + PAD), PAD) l:resize(tw, TAB_H) l:setStyleSheet(style(on and COL.tabon or COL.tab, on and COL.accent or COL.border)) l:echo(string.format( "
%s" .. " %d/%d
", on and COL.text or COL.dim, tw < 76 and SHORT[kind] or LABEL[kind], COL.dim, done, total)) l:show() end local t = SD.targets[SD.kind] or {} local top = PAD * 2 + TAB_H local ph = U.px(panel.container and (panel.container.get_height and panel.container:get_height() or panel.container.height)) -- what's left once the tabs, the selection line and the buttons are out.
